points.description: States the correct order explicitly: B, then C, then A (B least probable, A most probable), i.e. B < C < A.

Gives a valid justification covering both comparisons (B below C AND C below A): either B is a subset/special case/more specific than C and C is a subset/special case/more specific than A; or correct probabilities/formulas, e.g. P(B)=0.6^3*0.4^3≈0.0138, P(C)=C(6,3)*P(B)≈0.276, P(A)≈0.82 (rounding to 2 d.p. allowed; formula such as P(C)=20*P(B) is enough if the ordering is apparent).
points.partial_credit: Only 0.25 if the justification is correct for just one of the two comparisons (B vs C or C vs A) and contains no errors.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the order BCA stated correctly and a justification covering both B<C and C<A, using subset/specificity reasoning or correct calculations. A wrong order earns nothing for P1, and any wrong probability value or incorrect claim in the justification cancels P2. A justification for only one comparison earns 0.25; a bare order with no justification earns only P1.
